# MV2 of Munim, Inc.: free security and setup help for self-hosted AI

> Free, read-only checkers and tested fix pages for people who run AI on their own machines: Ollama, llama.cpp, Open WebUI, ComfyUI, vLLM, LiteLLM, n8n, Dify, RAGFlow, AnythingLLM, Langflow and Flowise. Advisory pages say which versions known security advisories affect and link each source. Made by MV2 of Munim, Inc. with AI agents; code is Apache-2.0.

Every page below is plain HTML. The browser checkers run entirely in the page and send nothing. General technical information, not professional security advice.

## Checkers and reports

- [Am I affected? CVE checker for Ollama, Open WebUI, vLLM, n8n, Dify, RAGFlow, AnythingLLM, Langflow, Flowise, LiteLLM, ComfyUI and MCP Inspector](https://munimv2.github.io/): Type your Ollama, Open WebUI, vLLM, n8n, Dify, RAGFlow, AnythingLLM, Langflow, Flowise, LiteLLM, ComfyUI or MCP Inspector version and see which known CVEs and advisories affect it, including advisories with no CVE ID or no fixed release that most scanners miss. Free, runs in your browser. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Will this local model fit my GPU? VRAM calculator for Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp](https://munimv2.github.io/fit.html): Estimate how much VRAM a local LLM needs at Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K, Q8_0 or F16 with your context length, and whether it runs fully on your GPU or spills to the CPU. Free, runs in your browser. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Which Ollama models fit a 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32 GB GPU? (October 2026)](https://munimv2.github.io/gpu-picks.html): Current Ollama models that run fully on the GPU for each VRAM size, with exact tags and download sizes from ollama.com: Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, gpt-oss, Qwen3, Llama 3.1. Plus the 32k default-context trap on 24 GB cards. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Sample local AI health check report (Ollama on a 4 GB GPU) | MV2 of Munim, Inc.](https://munimv2.github.io/sample-report.html): A real example of MV2's local AI health check ($49 for one machine, $199 for a small office): what's slowing an Ollama machine down, what's risky, and what to fix first, with exact commands. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.
- [Self-hosted AI in a small law office: a confidentiality check against ABA Opinion 512 and state bar guidance](https://munimv2.github.io/law-office.html): Running Ollama, Open WebUI or LM Studio in a law office keeps client text off cloud servers, but bar opinions, and from 1 January 2027 California's SB 574, still ask who can reach the server, what it keeps and who inside the firm can read it. What fifteen self-hosted AI tools let people reach out of the box, and nine concrete checks mapped to ABA Formal Opinion 512 and guidance from 26 states and DC, each linked to its primary source. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.

## Ollama

- [Ollama CVEs in 2026: is my Ollama version affected? (CVE-2026-103663, Bleeding Llama, CVE-2026-5757)](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama.html): Every 2026 Ollama CVE with the version that fixes it: CVE-2026-103663 (/api/pull path traversal, fixed in 0.35.0), CVE-2026-85180, CVE-2026-102697, the Windows updater CVEs and Bleeding Llama (CVE-2026-7482, fixed in 0.17.1). Plus what is known about CVE-2026-5757 and CVE-2026-15685, which name no fixed version. Check your version free. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Is my Ollama exposed? Lock down OLLAMA_HOST, Docker ports and Open WebUI (2026 checklist)](https://munimv2.github.io/secure-ollama.html): Ollama's API has no login. Check whether your Ollama is reachable from other machines, then fix it: OLLAMA_HOST on Linux, macOS and Windows, Docker -p 127.0.0.1, keeping Ollama internal behind Open WebUI, a Caddy proxy with basic auth or an API key, OLLAMA_ORIGINS, and Open WebUI sign-up settings. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.
- [Use Ollama from another computer or your phone without exposing it (SSH tunnel, Tailscale, LAN firewall)](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-remote-access.html): Reach your Ollama (or LM Studio) from a laptop or phone without opening it to everyone: an SSH tunnel, Open WebUI over Tailscale Serve, why tailscale serve in front of Ollama returns 403 and the two fixes, and a LAN-only firewall rule for Linux and Windows. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.
- [Ollama API key: your local Ollama has none. How to require one (Caddy or nginx) and connect Open WebUI, n8n and OpenAI clients](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-api-key.html): OLLAMA_API_KEY is for ollama.com, not your own server: the local API on port 11434 has no login. How to require a Bearer API key with Caddy or nginx (or use Open WebUI as the gate), test it, and connect Open WebUI, n8n, the OpenAI SDK and the ollama Python library. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.
- [Can any website talk to your local Ollama? One-click OLLAMA_ORIGINS check (also LM Studio CORS)](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-origins-check.html): A browser check, run on your own machine, that shows whether a website you visit could read and use your local Ollama (OLLAMA_ORIGINS set to *) or your LM Studio server with CORS on. Nothing is sent anywhere. How to fix it on Linux, macOS, Windows and Docker. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Open WebUI or n8n in Docker can't connect to Ollama? Fix it without exposing Ollama (2026)](https://munimv2.github.io/docker-ollama.html): Why Open WebUI, n8n, Dify or AnythingLLM in Docker get 'Connection refused', 'Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 11434)' or 'ECONNREFUSED ::1:11434', and four fixes for Docker Desktop and Linux that don't open Ollama to your whole network. With a one-line test. By MV2 of Munim, Inc.
- [Ollama slow or not using the GPU? Paste `ollama ps` and get the fix](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-gpu.html): Why Ollama runs on the CPU or is slow, and how to fix it: read the PROCESSOR column of ollama ps, NVIDIA driver minimums (550, or 570 for GTX 10-series), CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, Docker --gpus, context length, KV cache. Free, runs in your browser. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Ollama "Error: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:11434: bind: address already in use": Ollama is already running (safe fix)](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-address-in-use.html): What 'Error: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:11434: bind: address already in use' (Windows: 'Only one usage of each socket address') from ollama serve means, how to see what holds port 11434 on Linux, macOS and Windows, and why OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 is not the fix. Checked against Ollama's v0.40.15 source. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Ollama "Error: could not connect to ollama server, run 'ollama serve' to start it" on Linux: causes and fixes](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-could-not-connect.html): Why ollama list, pull or run print 'could not connect to ollama server, run 'ollama serve' to start it' on Linux and WSL: the systemd service is stopped, there is no systemd, OLLAMA_HOST points elsewhere, or Ollama is in Docker. Checked against Ollama's v0.40.15 source. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [ollama -v: "Warning: could not connect to a running Ollama instance" and "Warning: client version is": what they mean](https://munimv2.github.io/ollama-version-warning.html): What ollama -v means by 'Warning: could not connect to a running Ollama instance' and 'Warning: client version is', why the 'ollama version is' line (the server) is the version that security advisories are about, and how to find the second copy of Ollama. Checked against Ollama's v0.40.15 source. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## Open WebUI

- [Open WebUI security advisories 2026: is my version affected? (update to 0.13.0; GHSA-3vvh-g22g-jq6r is fixed in 0.12.2)](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui.html): Open WebUI 0.13.0 (3 November 2026) is the newest release and its notes say it has security fixes. Every advisory Open WebUI has published, including GHSA-3vvh-g22g-jq6r (18 October 2026), is fixed by 0.12.2. Free version check by MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Open WebUI behind nginx or Caddy: fix WebSocket and streaming errors without opening it up (WEBUI_URL, CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN, cookies)](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui-reverse-proxy.html): Open WebUI behind a reverse proxy: why WebSocket connections fail and streamed answers arrive garbled, and how to fix them with the right nginx or Caddy config and CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN, WEBUI_URL, secure cookies, WEBUI_SECRET_KEY and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, while keeping port 3000 off the network and sign-ups closed. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Open WebUI: "cannot be edited here while ENABLE_OAUTH_PERSISTENT_CONFIG is disabled", or your env change ignored? Persistent config](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui-env-ignored.html): Open WebUI says "These settings are read from environment variables and cannot be edited here while ENABLE_OAUTH_PERSISTENT_CONFIG is disabled", or you changed ENABLE_SIGNUP, WEBUI_URL, OLLAMA_BASE_URLS or ENABLE_API_KEYS in docker-compose and Open WebUI ignores it? After the first start, those settings come from its database (ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG defaults to True). Which settings this affects, a one-line check of whether sign-up is really off, and three fixes: Admin Settings, RESET_CONFIG_ON_START once, or ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [pip install open-webui: "Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement open-webui (from versions: none)": use Python 3.11 or 3.12](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui-pip-python.html): Why pip install open-webui fails with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement open-webui (from versions: none)' and 'No matching distribution found for open-webui': Open WebUI 0.13.0 only installs on Python 3.11 or 3.12. Tested with pip 26.3 on Python 3.10 to 3.14, with fixes for uv, venv and Docker. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Open WebUI SSO: "mismatching_state: CSRF Warning! State not equal in request and response" (causes and fixes)](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui-sso-mismatching-state.html): Open WebUI SSO sign-in fails with 'Sign-in with your identity provider failed' in the browser and 'mismatching_state: CSRF Warning! State not equal in request and response' in the log. Each cause reproduced with the libraries Open WebUI 0.13.0 uses, and how to tell which one you have. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Open WebUI: "String should match pattern '^\S+$'" when you edit a model or change its access (fix)](https://munimv2.github.io/openwebui-model-id-pattern.html): Open WebUI shows [object Object] or does nothing when you edit a model or change its access, and the 422 response says "String should match pattern '^\S+$'". Why model ids with spaces fail since 0.11.4, how to find them, and two fixes. Run with Open WebUI 0.13.0's own forms. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## llama.cpp

- [llama.cpp "image input is not supported - hint: if this is unexpected, you may need to provide the mmproj": the fix](https://munimv2.github.io/llama-cpp-image-input-not-supported.html): Why llama-server answers HTTP 500 'image input is not supported - hint: if this is unexpected, you may need to provide the mmproj', why every later message in the chat fails too (Open WebUI, AnythingLLM), and the two fixes: start llama-server with --mmproj, or turn off Vision for a text-only model. Reproduced with llama.cpp b12110. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## ComfyUI

- [ComfyUI --listen safely: use ComfyUI from another PC or your phone without opening it to everyone (2026)](https://munimv2.github.io/comfyui-listen.html): ComfyUI has no login, and --listen with no address opens port 8188 on every interface. Name the addresses instead (--listen 127.0.0.1,100.x.y.z), use Tailscale Serve, avoid --enable-cors-header, fix the 'non matching host and origin' 403 behind a proxy, keep ComfyUI-Manager's security_level, and update past the four CVEs fixed in 0.28.0. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## vLLM

- [vLLM security advisories: is my version affected? (update to 0.33.0; 0.32.0 is affected by 3 advisories)](https://munimv2.github.io/vllm.html): vLLM 0.33.0 (2 November 2026) is the newest release and is clear of all 123 advisories vLLM has published. 0.32.0 is affected by 3 advisories and 0.31.0 by 12. Check your vLLM version free. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [vLLM --api-key doesn't cover every endpoint: lock down vLLM with an allowlist proxy (Caddy or nginx)](https://munimv2.github.io/vllm-api-key.html): vLLM's --api-key only checks /v1, /v2, /inference and /cohere routes. /invocations, /tokenize, /pause, /abort_requests and /update_weights stay open, and vllm serve listens on every interface by default. How to bind vLLM to 127.0.0.1, allow only the endpoints your apps use through Caddy or nginx with a Bearer key, test it, and keep multi-node traffic private. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## LiteLLM

- [LiteLLM proxy hardening checklist: master key, LITELLM_SALT_KEY, Admin UI login, EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN and MCP stdio](https://munimv2.github.io/litellm-hardening.html): A self-hosted LiteLLM proxy holds every provider key you use. Checklist: update past GHSA-7hp6, a long master key that isn't the UI password, LITELLM_SALT_KEY set before you store models (and never changed), disable_env_credential_login, EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false, stdio MCP servers left off, port 4000 on 127.0.0.1 with the Admin UI and management routes reachable only from your network (Caddy or nginx), and tests. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [LiteLLM proxy advisories, October 2026: am I affected? (GHSA-w4c7-34wj-hqm8, GHSA-7hp6-4w63-5g45, GHSA-g5ff-637f-6q2m)](https://munimv2.github.io/litellm.html): LiteLLM's critical advisory of 27 October 2026, GHSA-w4c7-34wj-hqm8 (CVSS 10.0, proxies with an Enterprise licence), is fixed in 1.106.5, 1.105.6, 1.104.8 and 1.103.10. Check your LiteLLM version. Free, by MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## n8n

- [n8n security advisories, September to October 2026: is my n8n version affected? (3.0.1, 2.46.1, 2.45.5)](https://munimv2.github.io/n8n.html): n8n published 27 more security advisories on 14 and 28 October 2026, none with a CVE ID. Read per release line, every n8n advisory that names a fix is fixed in 3.0.1, 2.46.1 and 2.45.5. Check your n8n version. Free, by MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Self-hosted n8n security checklist (2026): the secure cookie error, reverse proxy, n8n audit, SSRF protection and webhook auth](https://munimv2.github.io/n8n-hardening.html): Harden a self-hosted n8n: fix 'configured to use a secure cookie' with HTTPS instead of N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false, keep port 5678 private, run n8n audit, keep the 2.0 defaults (Code node env access, Execute Command off), turn on N8N_SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED, protect webhooks, back up N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## Dify

- [Self-hosted Dify: which advisories affect my version? (before 1.16.0)](https://munimv2.github.io/dify.html): Self-hosted Dify before 1.16.0 is affected by 2026 advisories including unauthenticated SSRF (CVE-2026-105762), cross-workspace file reads with no CVE ID (GHSA-9c9q-5rj5-mjj2) and MCP server tampering (CVE-2026-105761). Dependency scanners don't check Dify's own version. Check yours free. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Self-hosted Dify security checklist: INIT_PASSWORD, the old public SECRET_KEY, open ports and default passwords](https://munimv2.github.io/dify-hardening.html): Self-hosted Dify (Docker Compose) checklist: set INIT_PASSWORD so a stranger can't claim /install; check whether your .env still has the published SECRET_KEY that .env.example shipped until 1.14.x; nginx, the plugin debugging port 5003 and some vector stores are published on every interface; console CORS is * because .env.example sets it; the bundled database, Redis, sandbox and plugin keys are public defaults. With commands and tests. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## RAGFlow

- [Self-hosted RAGFlow: which advisories affect my version? (0.27.2 has one with no fix)](https://munimv2.github.io/ragflow.html): RAGFlow 0.25.2 to 0.27.2, the latest 0.x release, lets any signed-in user run another user's private agent (GHSA-c6q8-23rp-32cv, no CVE ID). Its Python fix is in 1.0.0-rc1, whose default server is new Go code. Before 0.25.0, any signed-in user can run OS commands through Jinja2 templates. Check your version free. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## AnythingLLM

- [Self-hosted AnythingLLM: which advisories affect my version? (fixed in 1.16.2; most list a commit, not a version)](https://munimv2.github.io/anythingllm.html): AnythingLLM has 20+ GitHub advisories in 2026, but most list a commit hash or '>1.16.1' as the patched version, so scanners can't use them, and several are missing from OSV.dev. Before 1.16.2, anonymous visitors of an embedded chat widget can see the owner's private Memories; before 1.13.0, anyone who can chat with an agent can run commands in the container. Check your version free. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## Langflow

- [Langflow CVE-2026-105697 and the October 2026 advisories: am I affected?](https://munimv2.github.io/langflow.html): Langflow before 1.10.3 has OS command injection through MCP server settings (CVE-2026-105697, CVSS 9.9), reachable without an account when auto-login is on, the default for pip installs. Check your Langflow version for this and the other 2025-2026 advisories. Free, by MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Langflow security checklist: auto-login is off from 1.13.0 (LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD), LANGFLOW_SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS, CORS, port 7860](https://munimv2.github.io/langflow-hardening.html): Langflow 1.13.0 (22 October 2026) turned LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN off by default; before it, a pip-installed Langflow signed everyone in as superuser. How to set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD without losing your flows, LANGFLOW_SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS, CORS, secret key, code execution, port 7860. Checked against 1.13.0. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.
- [Langflow won't start: "Username and password must be set. Set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD before starting Langflow" (1.13 fix)](https://munimv2.github.io/langflow-superuser-password.html): Langflow 1.13.0 turned auto-login off by default, so startup fails with "Username and password must be set" until LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD is set. How to fix a new install, and how to upgrade from 1.12 without losing access to your flows. Checked on 2 November 2026. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## Flowise

- [Flowise is archived: 3.1.4 is the last release, and its six September advisories will never get a fix. What to do](https://munimv2.github.io/flowise.html): Flowise was archived on 13 August 2026 and no longer accepts security reports. Six advisories published on 10 September 2026 (two critical SSO takeovers, CVE-2026-100607 and CVE-2026-100606, and four missing-authorization bugs) affect 3.1.4, the final release, and no official fix will ship. OSV.dev's CVE records wrongly mark 3.1.4 as fixed. Two fixes were merged after 3.1.4 but never released. Check your version, mitigations for today, and how to plan a move. Free, by MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

## Code and data

- [local-ai-checkup](https://github.com/munimtechnologies/local-ai-checkup): the same checks as a single read-only Python script (`python3 local_ai_checkup.py --json`), Apache-2.0
- [local-ai-checkup agent skill](https://github.com/munimtechnologies/local-ai-checkup/blob/main/skills/local-ai-checkup/SKILL.md): tells a coding agent when and how to run the checkup and to change nothing without the user; install with `npx skills add munimtechnologies/local-ai-checkup`
- [ai-stack-advisories](https://github.com/munimtechnologies/ai-stack-advisories): the advisory data behind these pages as JSON (`advisories.json`), Apache-2.0
